questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is legally intoxicated. Driving a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Keep your friend busy with other activities.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Do not let an intoxicated friend ride a motorcycle. Instead, arrange another way for them to get home, distract them with other activities, ask them to stay until they are sober, and get other friends to help.

questions.question: What should you do to lower your chances of a crash?

options.text: Use turn signals when you change lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead while riding.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when you change lanes.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others, use your turn signals and lights, keep space between you and other vehicles, look 12 seconds ahead, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to sudden changes.

questions.question: Which of these should you NOT do for safety when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Increase your distance from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: For night riding, slow down, use your high beam headlight when there are no oncoming vehicles, and increase your following distance. Watch the headlights and taillights of vehicles ahead to help you see the road.

questions.question: What should you do to lower your chances of a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Look only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, stay visible, use turn signals and brake lights, keep space around your motorcycle, look ahead and around you constantly, and be prepared to avoid hazards.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, and stress make you drowsy and can affect your ability to ride safely. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all of your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT necessary for an eye or face shield to work well?

options.text: It must be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.
It must be free of scratches.
It must allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be scratch-free, able to resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you to be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes other drivers see you better. Use it day and night.

questions.question: Which sign shape is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are used for road rules like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. Follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your body and mind.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to stay safe. Position yourself to stay out of blind spots, see better, avoid hazards, and escape danger. Position yourself in a way that discourages other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: A helmet will not protect you well if:
questions.explanation: Your helmet should meet DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection to:

options.text: See if parked vehicles are entering traffic.
Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
See if someone is turning behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, use your mirrors to check for cars approaching from behind. They may not see you until it is too late.

questions.question: Use more space between you and other vehicles when:
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is usually good. Use more space when conditions make it take longer to stop, such as on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes and let them pass when it is safe. Speeding up only makes it more dangerous.

questions.question: How can you discourage other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: Give dirty looks to other drivers.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to fill the space. This leaves less room on each side and discourages drivers from trying to share the lane.

questions.question: In a group ride, put less experienced riders near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if leading.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in other positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: In a group, less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them closely.

questions.question: What sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. Change lanes and let them pass when safe. Riding faster only makes it more dangerous.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in fog?

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane to see better before passing another vehicle on its left?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing. This helps you see better and makes oncoming traffic see you more easily.

questions.question: A person drank 8 alcoholic drinks 4 hours ago. The body removes 1 drink per hour. How many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals 4 drinks remaining.

questions.question: How do you lean your motorcycle for a turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To lean your motorcycle for a turn, press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
